newsitem.title: CHINA: China to limit old-age fund investment to T-bonds.
newsitem.headline: China to limit old-age fund investment to T-bonds.

text.p: China will shortly promulgate rules governing expanding old-age pension funds, limiting their investment to treasury bonds, the China Securities News said on Thursday.
The rules would require all companies and organisations, including privately owned firms, to use the same system to establish old-age pension funds, the newspaper said.
Beijing is also working hard to formulate rules governing social insurance for unemployment workers, the newspaper said but gave no details.
China started to reform its welfare system in the 1980s to lighten the burden on the state, formerly responsible for everything.

Currently, major Chinese cities use a system in which employees of state firms are required to pay around five percent of their average salaries into old-age pension funds while firms pay 25 percent of their payroll to the funds.
Different cities also pay various minimum unemployment fees to those who lose jobs.
There are currently no national laws governing the revised social welfare system and practices vary greatly from one area to another.
